summary: Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, he was a visiting scholar at the University of Virginia in 1987. By 1988, he held a post as librarian at Tibet House in New Delhi.

Geshe Rabten was a Buddhist studies and Tibetology scholar. He studied at Sera Monastery (~1940–1959) and under Trijang Rinpoche (~1940–1981), and taught at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies from ~1964 to 1969.

A scholar of Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy, he studied at Dhargyey Monastery, Sera Monastery (1952–1959), and the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1971–1980). In 1978, he became a resident teacher at the Library of Tibetan Works and Archives.

Active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Sera Monastery (~1970–1987), Gyuto Monastery (~1988–1989), and under Geshe Thubten Rinchen. He taught at Kopan Monastery (~1990–1991) and became resident teacher at Jamyang Buddhist Centre in 1994.

A Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar, he studied under Ling Rinpoche and at Sera Monastery and Gyume Tantric College. He taught at both institutions, was a visiting lecturer at the University of Virginia (1999–2000), and directed Tibetzentrum Österreich (2008).
Geshe Tshondru Kongpel worked in the fields of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned Geshe degrees through his studies at Drepung Monastery and Yungdrung Ling Monastery.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Drepung Monastery (~1921–1938) and under Agvan Dorjiev. He taught at Columbia University (~1962–1974) and served at the Tibetan Buddhist Learning Center from ~1958 to 1983.
Geshe Yeshe Thabkhe is a scholar in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and philosophy. He held positions at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, attested between 1991 and 2019.

Working in Buddhist studies and Tibetology, he studied at Sera Monastery (~1938–1959) and under Geshe Lhundup Sopa, Geshe Lodoe Sangpo, and Chusang Rinpoche. He taught Buddhist philosophy at the Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies (~1967–1971).
Geshé Tenpa Tendzin was a scholar who pursued studies under the 14th Dalai Lama, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, and Trijang Rinpoche.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and philosophy, he studied at Otani University and under Manshi Kiyozawa. He had a long academic career at Otani University, serving as lecturer (1901), professor (1906–1911), and president (1924–1925).

A specialist in Iranian, Central Asian, and religious studies, Gnoli studied at Sapienza University of Rome. He taught at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" (1965–1993) and Sapienza (1993–2008), and directed IsMEO and its successor IsIAO (1979–2011).

An archaeology and Indology scholar, he studied at Aligarh Muslim University under C. F. Andrews, Mohammad Ishaq, and Nazir Ahmad Dehlvi. He held professorships at St. Stephen's, Rajshahi, and Lahore, and directed the Hyderabad Archaeological Department (~1914–1943).

A scholar in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, she studied under Raniero Gnoli and completed studies at the University of Naples "L'Orientale" and Sapienza University of Rome. Around 1998, she held a teaching post at "L'Orientale."
Specializing in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, Gianpaolo Vetturini earned his PhD at the University of London under the doctoral supervision of Tadeusz Skorupski.

A scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology, he studied at Kyoto University (~1911–1914). He served at Kyoto University as a lecturer (1929) and associate professor (1935–1948), and later held professorships at Rissho University and Aichi Bunkyo Women's College.
Giho Okada was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at Komazawa University under Kaiten Nukariya. He later served as a professor at Komazawa University.

A specialist in Iranian and Central Asian studies, linguistics, and Indology, Ito studied at Kyoto University under Atsuuji Ashikaga and Yasusaburo Sakaki. He served as professor at Kyoto University (1968–1972) and Kyoto Sangyo University (1977–1980).

A Buddhist studies scholar, Fronsdal earned a PhD at Stanford University (~1991–1998) under Carl Bielefeldt and Bernard Faure, among others. He has taught at the Sati Center for Buddhist Studies (~1997) and the Insight Meditation Center (~2001).
A researcher in Indology and religious studies who studied under Madeleine Biardeau, he was attested in 2004 as a senior fellow at the CNRS, an EHESS member, and an exchange program director at FMSH.
